42af297ccc.q: What did Doug Clifton Curling teach about redirecting employees who don't fit their current role?
42af297ccc.a: Doug taught the principle that sometimes you cannot make an orange into an apple. Instead, find out what that person does extremely well and what they love doing most—the thing they would do for free—and put them in that job in the company. If you do that, that person will add value; but if you keep trying to make the orange an apple, everyone ends up in trouble. This philosophy, applied across multiple companies, has led some former team members to rise to the executive level.

012917dfa2.q: How did Doug Clifton Curling respond when Mark Anthony Peterson wanted to fire an employee who threw a water bottle?
012917dfa2.a: Doug pulled Peterson aside and revealed context: the employee had lost his wife, was a single father raising three kids, and his identity was built on working directly with Doug. Though Doug gave Peterson full authority to fire him, he contextualized the situation with compassion. This awakening led Peterson to have a long conversation with the employee, discover what made him happy, and create a scenario where the employee could work on projects with his family around him and take on slow-fuse intellectual work. The employee's life improved significantly.

17b8c80b8f.q: What water and infrastructure projects did Doug Clifton Curling pursue after Choice Point was sold?
17b8c80b8f.a: After Choice Point was sold and Doug became extremely well off, he traveled to Central and South America digging wells so that underserved villages could have access to clean water. This work was purely driven by his mission to serve communities without any financial necessity, demonstrating his commitment to giving back and having fun while making a real difference.
